section.title: Overview
section.para: This module ships structured log entries from the Kamailio configuration script to a log server over HTTP. The entries are collected in batches and posted. The format of the request is selected with the format parameter, the supported formats are described in the section Formats.

Logging is asynchronous: the SIP worker processes only pack the values of the log entry and pass them to a dedicated sender process. The sender process serializes the entries to JSON, collects them in a queue and posts them in batches, so the SIP processing is never blocked by the HTTP transfer.

The set of fields of a log entry is described by log groups. A log group is defined with the default_map and map parameters and is referenced by its key as the first argument of the http_log() function. Fields of the default map are filled automatically (current time, route name, pseudo-variables, static values), fields of the map are filled from the arguments of http_log().

section.title: &kamailio; Modules
section.para:
The following modules must be loaded before this module:
pv - needed when pseudo-variables are used in default_map or in the text arguments of http_log(), which is the case in any practical configuration.

section.title: External Libraries or Applications
section.para:
The following libraries or applications must be installed before running &kamailio; with this module loaded:
libcurl.
The module is available only on Linux: the sender process is built on epoll and timerfd.

section.title: target (str)
section.para: URL of the ingestion endpoint of the log server, see the section Formats for the endpoint of each format. The parameter can be set multiple times to configure several targets, they are used in round-robin order with failover to the next target when a request fails.

para.emphasis: Default value is empty (at least one target is required).

section.title: format (str)
section.para: Format of the request and its options, in the form name[=>option=value[;option=value...]]. The name is one of elasticsearch or ndjson, the options are specific to the format and are described in the section Formats. A value containing commas or spaces has to be enclosed in single or double quotes. An unknown option is a configuration error. The parameter can be set only once, a second definition is a configuration error.

section.title: auth_username (str)
section.para: User name for HTTP basic authentication on the targets. The authentication is enabled when both auth_username and auth_password are set.

section.title: auth_password (str)
section.para: Password for HTTP basic authentication on the targets. See auth_username.

section.title: timeout (int)
section.para: Maximum duration of one HTTP request in milliseconds. A request that takes longer is treated as failed and the batch is retried on the next target.

section.title: chunked (int)
section.para: If set to 1, the request body is sent with chunked transfer encoding: the entries of a batch are serialized one by one while curl is sending, so only one entry at a time is kept in the request buffer. If set to 0, the whole batch is assembled in memory first and sent with a Content-Length header, for servers or proxies that do not accept chunked requests.

section.title: batch_size (int)
section.para: Maximum number of log entries in one HTTP request. When the number of queued entries exceeds this value, a request is sent immediately without waiting for batch_delay.

para.emphasis: Default value is 0 (no limit, the whole queue is sent in one request).

section.title: batch_delay (int)
section.para: Interval in milliseconds between the sending of the queued entries. The minimum value is 100.

section.title: queue_size (int)
section.para: Maximum number of log entries kept in the queue of the sender process. When the limit is exceeded (e.g. all targets are down), new entries are dropped, an error is logged and the log_http_drop_total statistic is incremented.

section.title: default_map (str)
section.para: Fields of a log group that are filled automatically on every http_log() call. The format of the value is described in the section Format of default_map and map parameters. The parameter can be set multiple times, once per log group.

section.title: map (str)
section.para: Fields of a log group that are filled from the arguments of the http_log() function. The format of the value is described in the section Format of default_map and map parameters. The parameter can be set multiple times, once per log group.

para.emphasis: Default value is empty (at least one map is required).

section.title: elasticsearch
section.para: Elasticsearch Bulk API, described in the Elasticsearch documentation: https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elasticsearch/operation/operation-bulk.
Options:

listitem.para: index - name of the index to put the entries in. The name may contain strftime() conversion specifiers, evaluated in UTC when a batch is sent, e.g. kamailio-%Y.%m.%d for daily indices. When not set, the index has to be part of the target URL.

section.title: ndjson
section.para: Newline delimited JSON: the body of the request is the JSON objects of the entries, one per line, with no envelope. See https://github.com/ndjson/ndjson-spec. The format is accepted by the log servers consuming a stream of JSON lines.
The format has no options.

section.title: Format of default_map and map parameters
section.para: The value of both parameters has the format key(name:type[, name:type ...]).

listitem.para: key - name of the log group, used as the first argument of http_log().
name - name of the JSON field in the log entry. Special field names of the log server (@timestamp, _msg, _time) can be used directly.
type - type of the field, see below.

section.para: Types allowed in default_map:

listitem.para: timestamp - current time in RFC3339 format with millisecond precision (UTC), e.g. 2026-10-06T08:09:41.123Z.
route_name - name of the route block from which http_log() is called.
$... - a pseudo-variable, its value is taken at the time of the call (e.g. $si, $ci, $var(x)). Null values result in the field being omitted.

section.para: Types allowed in map:

listitem.para: text - string. The argument may contain pseudo-variables, they are evaluated at the time of the call. Empty strings are omitted from the entry.
bool - boolean, the argument must be true, false or a number (non-zero is true).
inet - IPv4 or IPv6 address, stored as a string.
date - date and time in local time zone in the format %Y.%m.%d %H:%M:%S, stored in RFC3339 format (UTC).

section.para: Build a log entry of the log group key and pass it to the sender process. The number of values must be equal to the number of fields in the map of the group, and each value must match the type of the corresponding field. Up to 5 values can be given.
Returns 1 on success and -1 on error (unknown group, wrong number or type of values, sender process not reachable).
This function can be used from ANY_ROUTE.

example.title: http_log usage with Elasticsearch
http_log usage with ndjson format
example.programlisting: ... modparam("log_http", "target", "http://127.0.0.1:9428/insert/jsonline?_stream_fields=app,group") modparam("log_http", "format", "ndjson") modparam("log_http", "default_map", "gen(_time:timestamp, app:&kamailio, group:&gen, route:route_name, callid:$ci, src_ip:$si)") modparam("log_http", "map", "gen(_msg:text, code:num)") ... request_route { ... http_log("gen", "request $rm from $si", "100"); ... } ...

section.title: Queue algorithm
section.para: The sender process collects the log entries in a queue. Every batch_delay milliseconds, or as soon as the queue grows over batch_size entries, the first batch_size entries of the queue (the whole queue when batch_size is 0) are posted to the current target in one request. Only one request is in flight at a time.

On success (HTTP 2xx) the entries are removed from the queue and the next batch is sent immediately if the queue is not empty. On failure the log_http_err_total statistic is incremented and the same batch is retried on the next target. When all the targets failed, the entries stay in the queue until the next batch_delay tick.
When the queue holds more than queue_size entries, new entries are dropped and log_http_drop_total is incremented.
